newsitem.title: INDIA: India auto data tells rural income story-Capel B&K.
newsitem.headline: India auto data tells rural income story-Capel B&K.

text.p: Latest industry data on Indian automobile sales during October-December 1996 shows that the influence of agricultural incomes over manufacturing has risen significantly, James Capel B&K said on Thursday.
The securities firm said this signal reinforced its belief that the country's recent industrial slowdown was likely to be arrested in the last quarter of 1996.
Industrial growth slowed to 9.8 percent in April-September 1996, from 12.1 percent a year ago. Government figures for the fourth quarter of 1996 have not yet been released.

"The slowdown will be arrested because of higher demand for industrial goods due to higher rural incomes. Higher rural incomes would, in turn, lead to increased spending from other sectors through the multiplier effect," Capel B&K said in a note to investors.
The securities firm said the impact of rural incomes on demand was seen after the harvest beginning at the end of September.
"The rural market accounts for over 90 percent of tractor sales and above 60 percent of utility vehicles and motorcycle sales," Capel B&K said.

"All these three segments of the auto sector have registered higher growth in the third quarter of 1996/97 (April-March) compared to the third quarter of 1995/96 while the other segments have seen a deceleration in growth," the firm said.
Official auto figures were released earlier this month.
The securities firm said exceptionally good monsoon rains and high foodgrain prices would fuel a surge in rural incomes and demand.
"While agricultural growth will be above 4.0 percent, foodgrain prices have increased by 18 percent year-on-year as against only 3.7 percent for the manufacturing sector," It said.
"This indicates a substantial rise in farm incomes in real terms vis-a-vis manufacturing," it said.
But Capel B&K said the increased demand would not be spread over the entire industrial sector.
"The sectors that will see an increase in demand in the initial phase would be personal care, consumer durables, cement, paints, textiles and tobacco," it said.
